supersonic-jets.title: Supersonic Jets
supersonic-jets.snippet: Collimating a high-velocity plume of matter that identically exceeds the local speed of sound drives the formation of Supersonic Jets, transporting energy and momentum across galactic distances. fluids-nonlinear-overview.title: Fluid Dynamics and Nonlinear Systems
fluids-nonlinear-overview.snippet: The complex, dynamic behavior of continuous media and systems far from thermodynamic equilibrium is rigorously described by the Navier-Stokes equations, a set of non-linear partial differential equations that express the fundamental conservation of mass, momentum, and energy within a fluid flow. At the core of fluid dynamics is the continuum assumption, which posits that the macroscopic properties of a fluid—such as density, velocity, and pressure —can be treated as continuous fields, effectively averaging over the discrete molecular collisions described by Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics. The dynamical evolution of these fields is governed by the conservation of mass, expressed via the continuity equation, and the conservation of momentum, formulated in the Navier-Stokes equations.
